citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (2023). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University)
description: MMMU (Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning) is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering) across 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.
name: MMMU
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question was reviewed by a secondary review team for quality and guideline adherence. Difficulty levels were assigned by co-authors. No specific number of independent annotations per item is stated beyond the secondary review process.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in the relevant majors across 30 subjects. For human expert evaluation, 90 college senior students were selected to represent a wide range of experts in the corresponding 30 subjects (3 student experts per subject).
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom web interface developed by Tianyu Zheng for data annotation and verification
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected multimodal questions from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials. All questions must contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, and not be ambiguous. Questions were categorized as multiple-choice or open-ended. Annotators annotated all fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). Data was stored in JSON format. Annotators were instructed to avoid questions with easily accessible answers (e.g., selecting questions whose answers are in separate documents or at the end of textbooks) to mitigate data contamination. Strict adherence to copyright and licensing regulations was mandatory.
rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. Subjects like law and linguistics were excluded because it was difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems, potentially limiting coverage. Annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination concerns with foundation models. Questions are exclusively in English, limiting linguistic diversity.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected in three stages. First, 30 subjects from six disciplines were selected based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted. Second, over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and to select questions without immediately available answers (e.g., answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks). This process resulted in a diverse collection of approximately 13K questions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials. The raw collection comprised approximately 13K questions before quality filtering.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI as defined by Morris et al. There lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and "90th percentile of skilled adults," nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI on its own.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage data cleaning was performed: (1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. (2) Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format. (3) Authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset has a live-updating leaderboard available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard. The paper documents version changes (V1 through V4) with additions of new model results and corrections over time.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is intended to stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence. The benchmark is designed to monitor progress towards Expert AGI (Level 3 in Morris et al.'s taxonomy), which marks a critical milestone denoting AI that reaches "at least 90th percentile of skilled adults" in a broad range of tasks, with significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. The authors caution that MMMU is a necessary but not sufficient test for Expert AGI.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal foundation models on college-level multi-discipline understanding and reasoning tasks; benchmarking progress towards Expert AGI; assessing expert-level visual perception, domain knowledge recall, and deliberate reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models (LMMs); measuring three essential skills: perception, knowledge, and reasoning.

null_reasons.publisher: No single publishing organization is identified; the dataset is a collaborative effort across multiple universities and research institutions with no single publisher named.
null_reasons.license: No license is explicitly stated in the paper for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe (start/end dates) for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data, gaps, or unavailable observations in the dataset collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described; the dataset consists of curated questions with no missing value filling strategy.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, resampling, synthetic insertion) is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or formal annotation quality analysis (e.g., Cohen's kappa) are reported.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No ML models or automated tools were used in the annotation/labeling pipeline; annotation was performed manually by human annotators.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of college-level academic questions and images; no personal or sensitive information about individuals is collected. The annotation protocol explicitly states annotators should avoid collecting questions containing private information.
